facts.text: North San Pedro’s name honors Saint Peter, following Spanish colonial naming traditions for missions, creeks, and settlements.
The first permanent settlement in the area was the Santa Petronila Ranch, founded in 1762 by Captain Blás María de la Garza Falcón.
North San Pedro is the northern remnant of historic San Pedro barrio, annexed south in 1990, and now depends on Robstown for police, fire, water, gas, and electricity.
Geographically, North San Pedro sits at 27°48′10″N 97°40′59″W on the flat Gulf Coastal Plain, about 79 feet above sea level.
Spanish colonial ranchers from Nuevo Santander began establishing outposts in the 1760s north of the Rio Grande, shaping the region’s ranching heritage.
Oil discoveries in 1930 sparked local employment and infrastructure growth, leading Robstown to provide tax‑free police, fire, water, gas, and electricity to North San Pedro.
